{{Short description|Arrangement of hyperplanes}}
In mathematics, a '''supersolvable arrangement''' is a  [[Arrangement of hyperplanes|hyperplane arrangement]] that has a maximal [[Flag (linear algebra)|flag]] consisting of [[Modular lattice|modular]] elements.  Equivalently, the [[Arrangement of hyperplanes#The intersection semilattice and the matroid|intersection semilattice]] of the arrangement is a [[supersolvable lattice]], in the sense of [[Richard P. Stanley]].<ref>{{cite journal|mr=0309815|last=Stanley|first= Richard P.|
authorlink=Richard P. Stanley|title=Supersolvable lattices| 
journal=[[Algebra Universalis]]|volume= 2 |year=1972|
pages= 197–217|doi=10.1007/BF02945028|s2cid=189844197}}</ref> As shown by [[Hiroaki Terao]], 
a complex hyperplane arrangement is supersolvable if and only if its complement is fiber-type.<ref>{{cite journal| mr=0865835| 
last=Terao|first= Hiroaki|authorlink=Hiroaki Terao|title=Modular elements of lattices and topological fibration|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|volume= 62 |year=1986|issue= 2|pages= 135–154|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(86)90097-6 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

Examples include arrangements associated with [[Coxeter group]]s of type A and B.

The [[Orlik–Solomon algebra]] of every supersolvable  arrangement is a [[Koszul algebra]]; whether the converse is true is an open problem.<ref>{{cite journal|first=Sergey|last= Yuzvinsky|title= Orlik–Solomon algebras in algebra and topology|journal= [[Russian Mathematical Surveys]]|volume= 56 |year=2001|issue= 2|pages= 293–364|mr=1859708|doi=10.1070/RM2001v056n02ABEH000383|bibcode= 2001RuMaS..56..293Y}}</ref>
